title: Dashboard lane catalog and dynamic alert curves
content:
Purpose:
This doc collects a small catalog of dashboard "lanes" (high-level panels grouped by operator intent) and a proposal for dynamic alert curves that better reflect token-serving economics and bursty LLM traffic. The intent is pragmatic: give product and SRE owners a repeatable layout and an alerting pattern that avoids static thresholds that either never fire or flood paging during storms.

Scope and audience:
- Observability team + service owners for token-serving stacks (hosted API, Dedicated runtime).
- Not a full instrument spec; complements metric-instrumentation PRs.
- Focused on runtime, cost, and quality signals for production rollouts.

Design goals (brief):
- Operator-focused lanes: each lane is a distinct mental model (investigate latency regressions vs. understand cost trends).
- Low-cardinality top-level summaries with drilldowns for tenant/model level when needed.
- Alerts that are adaptive to baseline and burn rate rather than static percentiles.
- Cost-aware SLOs: surface cost per effective token and cold-cache behavior.

Lane catalog (operational lanes) — rough descriptions:
1) Latency Health (operator quick-check)
   - Purpose: fast determination of perceived latency issues.
   - Top widgets: p50/p90/p99 request latency (backend end-to-end), synthetic endpoint probe p99, error-rate-over-latency heatmap.
   - Drilldowns: model-level latency, sequence-length distribution, KV-cache hit rate overlay.

2) Throughput and Capacity (capacity planning + incident)
   - Purpose: see utilization and headroom of dedicated GPU pools and autoscale actions.
   - Top widgets: GPU utilization by pool, request queue depth, average batch size, scaling events timeline.
   - Notes: show reserved vs burst capacity and chargeback tags.

3) Cost & Token Economics (finance + infra ops)
   - Purpose: understand token unit costs and correlation to latency/quality.
   - Top widgets: tokens/sec, tokens-per-request, cost-per-1k-tokens (7d/30d), effective cost per successful-response (including retries/fallbacks).
   - Drilldowns: quantization profile usage and model-variant mix.

4) Error and Degradation (pager-first)
   - Purpose: quick triage for customer-facing failures.
   - Top widgets: 5xx rate, partial-response rate, model-fallback invocations, top error codes by route.
   - Include a compact runbook link per major error cluster.

5) Output Quality & Regression Signals (ML/product owners)
   - Purpose: early detection of quality regressions tied to rollout or quantization changes.
   - Top widgets: BLEU/ROUGE-like scores for eval set (daily), prompt-regression alert counts, hallucination-rate proxy (NER/confidence mismatch).
   - Notes: needs external eval harness to feed metrics.

6) Tracing breadcrumbs (developer deep-dive)
   - Purpose: session reconstruction and trace anchors for tokenized inference (synthetic trace snippets).
   - Top widgets: trace sampling rate, recent sampled traces list, KV cache timeline per trace.

Metric taxonomy (high level; single-line definitions — keep concise):
- request.count: number of inference requests accepted (tags: route, model, tenant). Frequency: 1s rollup.
- request.latency_ms: end-to-end request latency in ms (p50/p90/p99). Cardinality: low for top-level (no tenant by default).
- token.count: tokens produced per request and cumulative per minute.
- kvcache.hit_rate: ratio of KV cache hits to lookups per request.
- model.fallback.count: count of requests that triggered fallback to cheaper/resilient variant.
- gpu.utilization_pct: GPU utilization per pool.
- batch.size: average tokens per batch and requests per batch.
- error.5xx.count: server-side errors.
- synthetic.probe.latency_ms: synthetic probe latency (global and region).
- cost.per_1k_tokens_usd: rolling cost metric derived from billing and token counts.

Tracing guidance (practical rules):
- Span naming: service.operation.resource, e.g. serving.generate.model-ggml-13b.v1
- Attach these attrs to top-level request span: request.id, tenant.id (optional), model.id, route, seq_length_in, seq_length_out, kvcache.hits, batch.size, variant.reason (if fallback).
- Key semantic spans: request.receive, request.route, model.load (cold), model.forward, kvcache.lookup, response.assemble.
- Sampling: adaptive 0.1% baseline sampling, elevated sampling to 100% for requests that hit error. For sudden p99 latency spikes, auto-increase sampling for 10 minutes for the affected route/model.
- Trace size control: limit tokenized prompt content in span attributes (hash or pointer to KV store) to avoid PII leakage and large spans.

Dynamic alert curves (proposal):
Problem: static thresholds (eg p99 > 500ms) lead to noisy alerts during planned bursts and miss slow steady degradations.
Proposal pattern: alerts as functions over baseline and burn rate. Two inputs: baseline(value) = rolling 14-day median for this lane and sensitivity window s (e.g., 5m).
Alert types:
A) Relative spike alert:
   - Trigger when current p99 > baseline.p99 * k AND absolute p99 > floor_ms (k=1.6, floor_ms=200ms).
   - Suppression if synthetic.probe latency is within baseline (to avoid false positives from client-side).

B) Burn-rate alert (SLO-style):
   - Compute SLO error budget burn rate over 1h and 6h windows. Trigger when burn_rate > 4x expected AND sustained for 3 consecutive evaluation windows.

C) Cost spike alert:
   - Trigger when rolling 24h cost-per-1k-tokens increases by >30% vs rolling 7d baseline AND correlated with batch.size < expected OR increased fallback usage.

Curve tuning knobs to expose in dashboard controls: baseline window, k multiplier, minimum absolute floor, sensitivity window.

Examples (informal):
- If p99 jumps to 2x baseline for 10m but synthetic probe is fine, route-specific breakpoint: likely tenant-traffic skew; escalate to routing team, not immediate page.
- If burn rate > threshold and p99 elevated: page SRE immediately.

Runbooks and operational playbook notes (short):
- First pass: check synthetic probes + global p99. If probes good but user p99 bad -> check tenant-specific throttles, routing decisions, KV cache per-tenant stats.
- Second pass: check GPU pool scaling events and queue depth. If queue depth growing with batch.size decreasing -> degraded scheduling.
- Third pass: inspect sampled traces for model.load spans (cold loads) and fallback invocations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to surface per-tenant cost signals without leaking customer data on public dashboards? (option: obfuscate tenant ids and show top-N anonymized).
- Determine cardinality limits for top-level dashboards; propose 3 tenant drilldowns per panel.
- Implement lightweight baseline computation in telemetry pipeline (currently done in dashboard queries — consider precomputed Baseline metric).
- Evaluate whether probe suppression rules miss certain edge cases (e.g., region-specific network issues).

Quick implementation plan (MVP):
- Instrument missing metrics: batch.size, kvcache.hits, cost.per_1k_tokens_usd (owned by billing-pipeline). Owner: Arjun Mehta. ETA: 3 weeks.
- Build 6 lane dashboards in Grafana with templated variables for model and route. Owner: Lena Fischer. ETA: 4 weeks.
- Wire dynamic alert curve as alertmanager rules using stored baseline queries and evaluate false-positive rate for 2 weeks. Owner: SRE rotation.

Notes to self / context snippets:
- Keep top-level dashboards slow-query-friendly: cache panel queries and use pre-aggregated rollups where possible.
- We should sync with billing team once cost-per-1k_tokens pipeline is available — link above.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: Dashboard Standards (see linked_artifacts).
- Jira: ENGOBS-412 is the baseline computation epic.

Comments welcome — this is intentionally light-on-formatting. Ping in #obs-dashboards for quick reviews.
